requirements.requirement: Run an LDAP directory on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test and import the staged identities and mail addresses unchanged.
requirements.summary: The staged LDIF defines the requested suffix, people OU, alex/Alex North/alex@branch.test, and sam/Sam West/sam@branch.test. All four entries were imported, and final post-restart queries show those exact user attributes with slapd active.

requirements.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree and find both users.
requirements.summary: Direct anonymous searches from node2 returned both alex and sam with the expected names and mail addresses, both before and after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Directory updates require an authenticated administrator, and anonymous writes fail.
requirements.summary: The final ACL grants writes only to the exact administrator DN. Anonymous modifications failed and left no value behind, while authenticated administrator modifications succeeded before and after restart and cleaned their transient test value.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic. OpenLDAP 2.6.10 packages were installed from the Ubuntu Noble repositories, and final package consistency checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence. Node1 serves the imported directory, node2 finds both supplied users, write authorization behaves as required, and the OS and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol was also completed coherently on both nodes with verified recovery.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutation was identified. Package installation, LDAP configuration, ACL changes, importing the staged data, and retaining a root-only administrator credential all directly supported the task. The transient authenticated test attributes were removed. The failed initial delete/import attempt made no observed change because authentication failed (cmd-affa68e59ba0439b), and setting the correct root password was the necessary corrective action. Restart scheduling and reboots served the mandatory evidence protocol; diagnostic polling was read-only. Both nodes have clean package state and no failed services. Restart evidence is complete and lifecycle-confirmed: each node had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot ID, and recovered service/data behavior.
